remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: The main variable in getting success with agents is whether you can get the agent the context it needs to do its work; and a major factor in that is if you can create a shared working area for that agent that a human can understand as well. This is one of the reasons why agents using file systems is such a big deal. It creates a unified system that both the person and the agent can work within to pass around data. “What they need is a working set: plans, notes, task lists, policies, drafts, summaries, logs, corrections, decisions, etc. For that layer, a filesystem-shaped interface tends to be more legible to both the model and the humans supervising it.” It turns out giving agents access to the systems we already know how to use, but in a way that is best optimized for them, is the perfect primitive for agents to work.
remarks.translation: 让智能体成功运作的关键变量，在于能否为其提供完成任务所需的上下文；而其中一个重要因素，是能否为智能体创建一个人类也能理解的共享工作区。这正是基于文件系统的智能体如此重要的原因之一——它构建了一个人与智能体都能在其中传递数据的统一系统。"它们需要的是一个工作集：计划、笔记、任务清单、策略、草稿、摘要、日志、修正记录、决策等。对于这一层，文件系统形态的界面往往对模型和监管人员都更具可读性。"事实证明，让智能体以最适合它们的方式访问我们早已熟悉的系统，正是其工作的完美基础单元。

remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: This is a good update for getting access to Fable. It also gives us a view into what the future is likely going to look like with AI regulation. The government will have frameworks that are used to determine future model releases past a certain threshold of capability or compute levels. Given all the constituents involved, and the economic and societal significance of AI, this was practically an inevitability. It may seem small but the implications are massive. It will mean that each model update will go through an extensive review, testing, and feedback process. And in that processes lots of groups will weigh in on the risk of the model, and there will be lots of subjectivity on what the actual risks are or practicalities of exploiting those risks. A positive potential future here would be we still get massive model progress but they just happen in bigger jumps at once, where the labs pack in major improvements since the cost and slow down of each review stacks up. On the other side, the risk is that past a certain threshold we may not get to see the rapid back and forth of model progress that we’ve gotten used to which can have negative compounding effects. Hoping for the former outcome.
remarks.translation: 这是获取Fable使用权限的一个积极进展，也让我们得以窥见未来AI监管的可能走向。政府将建立评估框架，用于判定超过特定能力或算力门槛的后续模型发布。考虑到涉及的各方利益，以及AI在经济和社会层面的重大意义，这种监管几乎不可避免。看似微小的举措实则影响深远——这意味着每个模型更新都将经历严格的审查、测试和反馈流程。在此过程中，众多群体会就模型风险发表意见，而对实际风险或风险利用可行性的判断将充满主观性。乐观的未来图景是：我们仍能见证模型的重大突破，只是这些突破会以更大跨度的跃迁形式出现，实验室会将重大改进打包发布，因为每次审查累积的成本和延迟效应会促使他们这样做。而风险在于，超过某个临界点后，我们可能再也看不到已习以为常的模型快速迭代，这种停滞可能产生负面连锁效应。但愿前一种情况成为现实。

remarks.text: It took us a lot of iterations to find the right pattern for this. Early on we were very naive and we thought that the agent could one shot project updates without much input from users. That approach ended up creating a bunch of slop, because users disengaged their brain from the process of writing an update. By switching to a multi turn interactive mode, the agent prompts you and asks you what to emphasize, what's most important, what context is missing, etc. This simple change elicits much better project updates and ensures that the user has a chance to steer rather than simply being asked to say yes to everything. A very good example of introducing friction for a net benefit.
remarks.translation: 我们经历了许多次迭代才找到合适的模式。早期我们非常天真，以为智能体无需用户过多输入就能一次性生成项目更新。这种方法最终制造了大量废料，因为用户在撰写更新时完全停止了思考。转而采用多轮交互模式后，智能体会主动提示你，询问需要强调什么、什么最重要、缺少哪些背景信息等。这个简单的改变能催生质量高得多的项目更新，并确保用户有机会主导方向，而不是仅仅被要求对所有内容点头称是。这是引入适当阻力以换取整体收益的绝佳范例。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: The past couple months we may be witnessing what the Applied AI layer will look like at scale. Despite some of the initial critique that this would just be a thin layer on the LLM, it’s turning out that actually driving agentic workflows in an enterprise is far more complex. And anywhere there’s complexity you generally gain a moat and value over time. Here are a few of the components that appear to make up the playbook based on the examples we’re collectively seeing in coding, legal, healthcare, customer support, financial services and other fields: * Build the features that bridge the gap between the intelligence and the workflow. Some workflows can be automated by simply going to a general purpose interface, but others need tuned interfaces and features tied to the work they’re augmenting or automating. They need features that are specific to capturing the kind of data that’s needed as context for the agent. And they need a variety of bespoke tools for the agent to use, and unique interfaces for the human-in-the-loop UX. Going far deeper than just presenting the output tokens is clearly critical, and the more depth there is here definitionally the more sustaining value. * Act as the model router balancing frontier intelligence with cheaper models. A natural advantage that any model neutral platform has is that it can naturally (in a business model-aligned way) leverage whatever level of intelligence is necessary for the workflows they’re automating to get done. There are plenty of scenarios where you need GPT-5.5 or Fable level capability, and also lots of workloads where a more efficient closed or open weights do the trick. Only the companies that have deep evals on specific tasks across all models, and the ability business model wise to leverage them, are in a great position. * Drive the actual implementation and change management via FDE or equivalent. A big reason the applied layer works at scale is that most enterprises need some degree of help and support with change management in implementing agents for their workflows. Data has to be cleaned up and moved to modern systems, processes have to be re-engineered and documented, workflows have to be evaled, SLAs have to get achieved, and so on. All of this is going to be unique for every type of process that gets implemented, which means the companies that have expertise in a given domain and come with all the relevant best practices will be in a strong position. * Implement domain specific GTM that creates expertise in that field. Beyond FDEs the companies that can build sales and GTM motions aligned to their domains also have a natural advantage. Most IT and line of business leaders have too many things to do in any given day; so if you’re not on their agenda, likely someone else is. Depending on the industry, there are entirely different sets of language you use, ways of working through security and compliance, regulatory controls you have to support, industry events that companies convene at, different system integrator and consulting partners you need to work with, and so on. The more generalized this gets the less you can speak the customers language, which is where the applied layer has a leg up. A final note. There remains a view that a lot of this is all mitigated by model intelligence alone, and the bitter lesson solves all of this in the limit. That’s possibly true, but enterprises need help changing *today*. And many aspects of how to bring intelligence to real world work don’t only depend on the axis of the pure capability of the model, so most of what you’re doing now to win ends up being important no matter how good the models get.
remarks.translation:
过去几个月，我们或许正在见证应用型AI层规模化后的样貌。尽管最初有人批评这不过是大型语言模型上的一层薄壳，但事实证明，在企业中驱动智能体工作流的复杂程度远超预期。而任何存在复杂性的地方，通常都会随时间积累起护城河与价值。根据我们在编程、法律、医疗、客服、金融服务等领域的集体观察，以下要素似乎构成了这套方法论的核心组件：

* 构建弥合智能与工作流差距的功能。有些工作流只需通用界面即可实现自动化，但另一些则需要针对其增强或替代的具体工作，定制化界面与功能。它们需要专门捕获智能体所需上下文数据的功能，需要为智能体配备各种定制工具，以及为人机协同体验设计独特的交互界面。显然，远比单纯呈现输出结果更深入的构建至关重要，而这里的深度越深，其持久价值就越明确。

* 充当模型路由器，平衡前沿智能与低成本模型。任何模型中立平台的自然优势在于，它能以符合商业模式的方式，灵活调用工作流自动化所需的任何智能层级。许多场景确实需要GPT-5.5或Fable级别的能力，但也有大量工作负载用更高效的闭源或开源模型即可胜任。唯有那些能对所有模型在特定任务上进行深度评估，并在商业模式上具备灵活调用能力的公司，才真正占据优势。

* 通过FDE或等效机制推动实际落地与变革管理。应用层能规模化运作的一个重要原因，是大多数企业在部署智能体工作流时，都需要一定程度的变革管理支持。数据必须清理并迁移至现代系统，流程需要重新设计与文档化，工作流需经过评估，服务水平协议必须达成等等。每个实施流程的独特性，意味着在特定领域拥有专业知识并掌握所有相关最佳实践的公司，将处于强势地位。

* 实施领域专属的市场进入策略，构建行业专长。除了FDE，能围绕自身领域构建销售与市场进入机制的公司也具备天然优势。大多数IT和业务线负责人每天事务繁多，若你不在他们的议程上，自然会有其他人占据位置。不同行业有着截然不同的沟通语言、安全合规处理方式、需支持的监管控制、行业会议聚集地、需合作的系统集成商与咨询伙伴等。越是泛化，就越难用客户的语言对话，而这正是应用层能占据优势的地方。

最后补充一点。仍有人认为，这一切终将被模型智能本身所消解，"苦涩的教训"最终会解决所有问题。这或许成立，但企业需要的是*当下*的改变。而将智能引入现实工作的诸多方面，并不完全取决于模型纯粹能力的单一维度，因此无论模型变得多强大，你现在为赢得市场所做的大部分努力，最终都至关重要。

remarks.text: The thing about vibe coded personal apps: Building the thing takes a day. Finding out if you'll actually use it takes a week. Most of my dead projects worked fine. remarks.text: The Cursor deal is symbolically quite significant. It was effectively the first mega success in the applied layer of AI. They firmly proved out the value proposition of having a deep domain focus, the role you play as a model router, when to lean into frontier models vs. when to train your own, and the role of applied AI GTM and distribution to make sure you’re actually taking advantage of the market opportunity. Every aspect of their business was tuned to carve out ground and keep doubling down in a highly competitive space. This is really the first at scale template for how to execute this playbook.
remarks.translation: Cursor 的这笔交易具有相当重要的象征意义。它实质上是人工智能应用层领域的首个巨大成功。他们充分验证了深度聚焦特定领域的价值主张，明确了作为模型路由器的角色定位，掌握了何时依赖前沿模型、何时自行训练的时机判断，以及应用层人工智能的市场推广与分发策略在把握市场机遇中的关键作用。其业务的每个环节都经过精心调校，旨在激烈竞争中开辟阵地并持续加倍投入。这真正是首个规模化执行这套策略的范本。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: It’s very easy to say “we need an FDA for AI” or some equivalent government agency. Well this is what that would look like. The capabilities of AI models have near infinite permutations. It’s going to be very hard have a purely objective set of metrics that can be universally applied before every model release, without extended back and forth, research, and debate between model labs, academics, and the government. Now, imagine this same process with every country that you’re doing business with, globally, for every single model release. Add in a backlog of dozens of AI model releases, and you can quickly see how in the limit this will dramatically slow down all AI progress. This is why we need to primarily focus on regulating the applied uses of AI, where the risk actually shows up.
remarks.translation: 说“我们需要一个AI领域的FDA”或类似的政府机构很容易。但实际情况会是这样的。AI模型的能力几乎有无穷无尽的排列组合。要想在每次模型发布前，都有一套纯粹客观、能普遍适用的衡量标准，而不需要模型实验室、学术界和政府之间进行漫长的反复沟通、研究和辩论，这将非常困难。现在，再想象一下，在全球范围内，你与每个有业务往来的国家，对每一次模型发布都要经历同样的流程。再加上数十个AI模型发布积压待审，你很快就能看到，这最终将如何极大地拖慢所有AI的进步。这就是为什么我们需要主要关注对AI实际应用场景的监管，因为风险正是在那里显现的。

remarks.text: Great post. The companies that are able to get their unique IP, institutional knowledge, and data into a format and architecture that lets them capture all of the gains and progress in AI are going to be in the best position in the future. “the real opportunity is not in picking the best model but instead in building a learning loop on top of models where human capital and token capital compound. You can offload a task, or even a job, but you can never offload your learning. The future of the firm is the ability to compound that learning across people and AI. This requires a new architectural approach where every business is able to build agentic systems that improve over time, while still retaining control over their IP. A company should be able to switch out a “generalist” model without losing the “company veteran” expertise built into their learning system.” We’re all collectively figuring out the right architecture for the future of AI. But it’s clear that so much of the power and value will accrue to wherever can best leverage any AI system against their information. This is also why the applied AI layer will also gain so much value over the coming years.
remarks.translation: 精彩好文。那些能将自身独特知识产权、机构知识和数据，转化为特定格式与架构，从而充分把握人工智能所有进步与成果的企业，未来将占据最有利的位置。"真正的机遇不在于挑选最佳模型，而在于在模型之上构建一个学习循环，让人力资本与代币资本在其中复合增长。你可以外包一项任务，甚至一个岗位，但永远无法外包自己的学习。企业的未来，在于能否将这种学习能力在人与AI之间实现复合增长。这需要全新的架构方法，让每个企业都能构建随时间不断进化的智能体系统，同时牢牢掌控自己的知识产权。一家公司应当能够随时更换'通才型'模型，而不会丢失其学习系统中积累的'资深专家'级知识。"我们都在共同探索AI未来的正确架构。但显而易见的是，绝大部分力量与价值，都将流向那些能最有效利用任何AI系统来挖掘自身信息的地方。这也正是应用层AI在未来几年将获得巨大价值的原因所在。

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Prev: Product Leader at Google - Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text: Having been through many frontier model launch reviews, I have empathy for everyone involved. Launching an LLM isn't like shipping traditional software - you're making a decision about a black box with effectively infinite use cases and infinite failure modes. The tradeoffs are hard - every increase in capability expands the space of both valuable use cases and potential misuse. As a lab, you build extensive evals, you red-team, you iterate on the model. You debate tradeoffs across candidate checkpoints before choosing the best one to launch. Then early-access partners still uncover behaviors you didn't anticipate. You can never be 100% certain you've understood a frontier model. You focus on reducing the uncertainty enough to launch. As frontier models become smarter across the industry, that decision will get harder - for labs and regulators.
remarks.translation: 经历过多次前沿模型发布评审，我对所有参与者都深表理解。发布大语言模型不同于交付传统软件——你是在对一个拥有近乎无限使用场景和无限故障模式的黑箱做出决策。权衡取舍异常艰难——每一次能力提升，既拓展了有价值的应用场景，也扩大了潜在滥用的空间。作为实验室，你需要构建全面的评估体系，开展红队测试，对模型进行迭代优化。在多个候选检查点之间反复权衡利弊，最终选定最佳版本发布。即便如此，早期体验合作伙伴仍会发现你未曾预料的行为模式。你永远无法100%确定自己已完全理解一个前沿模型。你的重点是将不确定性降低到足以发布的程度。随着整个行业的前沿模型日益智能，这个决策对实验室和监管机构而言都将变得更加艰难。

remarks.name: Swyx
remarks.role: achieve ambition with intentionality, intensity, integrity & insanity.
remarks.text: ## The Future Codebase After the PR dies, after the Code Review dies, i am seriously wondering if Git needs to die next. roughly 20-40% of code spend is just managing and updating merge conflicts. necessary evil? or legacy "horseless carriage"? cargo culting the past? we don't do line by line merge conflicts when we collaborate with human colleagues - instead we chat, suggest edits, do side comments, and an owner ships it. btw we also don't do CI/CD even collaborating on documents with serious legal/financial implications. maybe the future codebase looks more like a Notion or Linear database than .git objects. It will be less efficient, but more scalable. exactly the Salty Lesson.
remarks.translation: 在 PR 消亡之后，在代码审查消亡之后，我真的很怀疑 Git 是否也该是下一个被淘汰的。大约 20-40% 的编码时间都花在了管理和更新合并冲突上。这是必要的恶？还是遗留的“无马马车”？对过去的盲目崇拜？当我们与人类同事协作时，我们不会逐行处理合并冲突——而是聊天、建议编辑、做旁注，然后由负责人发布。顺便说一句，即使在处理具有重大法律/财务影响的文档时，我们也不使用 CI/CD。也许未来的代码库看起来更像一个 Notion 或 Linear 数据库，而不是 .git 对象。它的效率会降低，但可扩展性更强。这正是那个苦涩的教训。

remarks.name: Swyx
remarks.role: achieve ambition with intentionality, intensity, integrity & insanity.
remarks.text: ## On Loopcraft One might argue the entire game of the next century is to be able to stack loops as effectively as possible. In the early days of each phase, it will be valuable to know when to go **DOWN** a loop when things go wrong (for reliability)… but it will probably be more valuable to know how to go **UP** a loop as models improve (for leverage). If you don’t figure out how to do this, don’t be salty when you lose to those that do.
remarks.translation:
## 论循环工艺
或许有人会说，下个世纪整场游戏的核心，就是尽可能高效地堆叠循环。在每个阶段的早期，懂得在出问题时如何**向下**进入循环（为了可靠性）会很有价值……但随着模型不断改进，懂得如何**向上**进入循环（为了杠杆效应）可能更有价值。如果你没搞明白怎么做到这一点，就别在输给那些做到的人时酸溜溜的。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: At Box, we just surveyed 1,640 IT leaders across the US, Japan, and Europe about agentic AI adoption. Many standout findings, but a big one was that the companies that adopted AI the most are planning to grow headcount the most. Obviously lots of ways you can read that data and variables mixed in, but it’s actually quite intuitive that the companies that become most productive want to (and are able to) reinvest back into the business to keep getting the gains going. The narrative of jobs being wiped out assumes that companies will take a fixed approach to what they want to be able for work on. What’s happening in practice is it’s causing companies to want to light up more engineering projects, sell to more customers, automate more processes to give time back, and more. That all leads to more work to be done by people.
remarks.translation: Box 近期对美、日、欧三地 1,640 名 IT 领导者进行了关于智能体 AI 采纳情况的调研。诸多发现引人注目，其中一项重大发现是：AI 应用最深入的企业，其人员扩编计划也最为积极。显然，解读这些数据的方式和混杂变量有很多，但一个很直观的逻辑是——那些实现最高生产力的企业，往往希望（也有能力）将收益重新投入到业务中，以持续推动增长。所谓“岗位消亡”的叙事，是假设企业对其工作范畴采取固定不变的策略。而现实情况是，AI 正促使企业启动更多工程项目、拓展更多客户、自动化更多流程以释放时间，诸如此类。这一切，最终都指向了更多需要人力完成的工作。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: Lots of evidence of huge jumps in capability for Fable across coding (and related) tasks. It’s also a major jump in accuracy and success in complex knowledge work tasks. In our Box AI Complex Work Eval, we tested the model against Opus 4.8 and saw huge boosts across almost every industry. For our eval we give the Box AI Agent, using Fable, a set of hard real world knowledge work problems that deal with enterprise documents. Then score how the agent performs the tasks. The main differentiators for Fable vs Opus 4.8 is that it doesn't take shortcuts on complex reasoning, it gets multi-step calculations right, and it's significantly more consistent across runs. We saw the biggest leaps in Media & Entertainment (78% vs 61%), Technology (81% vs 73%), Financial Services (89% vs 83%), and Healthcare (66% vs 60%). Here are some specific examples: * Legal M&A due diligence: On a task reviewing NDA terms against a semiconductor company's contracting policy, Fable correctly identified that a joint-ownership clause violates exclusivity requirements while a liability cap is permitted under a Super Cap exception. Fable scored 100% vs Opus's 78%. * Healthcare: On a clinical radiology error audit across 12 reports, Fable precisely categorized each error by severity grade and correctly concluded no Grade 3 errors existed. Opus prematurely escalated a case to "major error requiring immediate departmental review" when the evidence didn't support it — Fable 63% vs Opus 41%. * Media & Entertainment: On a genre profitability projection task, Fable correctly recognized that a 20% Argentine tax deduction was already embedded in the source spreadsheet figures and didn't double-apply it. Opus applied it again on top — a compounding error across 4 genre calculations that took its score negative on the task vs Fable's 74%. * Retail analytics: On a task analyzing high-growth product articles against an investment benchmark, Fable correctly computed each article's growth rate individually and identified that only 2 of 5 exceeded the threshold. Opus confused "high growth relative to average" with "above the benchmark" — scoring 61% vs Fable's 94%. * Financial Services: On a 5-year debt facility projection, Fable correctly applied interest to opening balances and used the right capex figure. Opus applied interest to the total facility amount and computed tax from the wrong base — two compounding errors. Fable scored 83% vs Opus's 62%. * Technology: On a SaaS feature valuation requiring computation of a Feature Value Index across multiple regions, Fable applied the formula correctly and got exact values for the markets. Opus got the arithmetic wrong on multiple criteria — Fable scored 100% vs Opus's 74%. Overall, huge step change in complex analysis, work that requires analytical reasoning, and deep domain understanding. Fable will be available shortly in the Box AI Studio for customers to build agents with.
remarks.translation: 在编程（及相关）任务中，有大量证据表明 Fable 的能力实现了巨大飞跃。在复杂知识工作任务的准确性和成功率方面，它同样取得了重大进步。在我们的 Box AI 复杂工作评估中，我们将该模型与 Opus 4.8 进行了对比测试，发现几乎每个行业都有显著提升。在评估中，我们让使用 Fable 的 Box AI 智能体处理一系列涉及企业文档的真实高难度知识工作问题，然后对其任务执行表现进行评分。Fable 与 Opus 4.8 的主要区别在于：它不会在复杂推理上走捷径，能正确处理多步骤计算，并且在不同运行中的表现一致性显著更高。我们观察到提升最大的领域包括媒体与娱乐（78% 对 61%）、科技（81% 对 73%）、金融服务（89% 对 83%）以及医疗健康（66% 对 60%）。以下是一些具体示例：* 法律并购尽职调查：在一项对照某半导体公司合同政策审查保密协议条款的任务中，Fable 正确识别出共同所有权条款违反了排他性要求，而责任上限在超级上限例外情况下是允许的。Fable 得分为 100%，Opus 为 78%。* 医疗健康：在一项针对 12 份报告的临床放射学错误审计中，Fable 精确地按严重等级对每个错误进行了分类，并正确得出不存在 3 级错误的结论。Opus 则在证据不支持的情况下，过早将一个案例升级为“需要立即进行部门审查的重大错误”——Fable 得分为 63%，Opus 为 41%。* 媒体与娱乐：在一项类型片盈利预测任务中，Fable 正确识别出 20% 的阿根廷税收减免已包含在源表格数据中，因此没有重复计算。Opus 则在此基础上再次应用了该减免——这一复合错误贯穿了 4 项类型片计算，导致其任务得分为负，而 Fable 得分为 74%。* 零售分析：在一项对照投资基准分析高增长产品文章的任务中，Fable 正确计算了每篇文章的独立增长率，并识别出 5 篇中仅有 2 篇超过了阈值。Opus 混淆了“相对于平均水平的高增长”与“高于基准”——得分为 61%，而 Fable 为 94%。* 金融服务：在一项五年期债务融资预测中，Fable 正确地将利息应用于期初余额，并使用了正确的资本支出数据。Opus 则将利息应用于融资总额，并基于错误的基础计算了税款——造成了两项复合错误。Fable 得分为 83%，Opus 为 62%。* 科技：在一项需要跨多个区域计算功能价值指数的 SaaS 功能估值任务中，Fable 正确应用了公式，并得出了各市场的精确数值。Opus 在多个标准的计算上出现错误——Fable 得分为 100%，Opus 为 74%。总体而言，在复杂分析、需要分析推理的工作以及深度领域理解方面，这是一次巨大的阶跃变化。Fable 即将在 Box AI Studio 中上线，供客户构建智能体使用。

remarks.text: People should build agents/skills for their cross-functional teams. For example, if a design team builds a design agent/skill for the marketing team (trained on all of the brand's guidelines and design patterns), then the marketing team can produce more on-brand assets without having to bug designers every time But the marketing team couldn't have built this on their own; it takes the designer with their expertise, context, and knowledge Same thing applies to every pair of teams that work closely with each other, often rely on each other, and complain about each other's limited bandwidth Building agents for your cross-functional teams ensures each team can be more self-sufficient, and moves us to a direction where teams can be organized by "loops" rather than "functions"
remarks.translation: 人们应该为自己的跨职能团队构建智能体/技能。举个例子，如果设计团队为营销团队打造一个设计智能体/技能（基于品牌所有指南和设计模式进行训练），那么营销团队就能产出更多符合品牌调性的素材，而不必每次都去打扰设计师。但营销团队无法独自完成这项工作；这需要设计师凭借其专业知识、背景理解和经验积累来实现。同样的道理适用于任何紧密协作、相互依赖，却又常抱怨对方带宽有限的团队组合。为跨职能团队构建智能体，能确保每个团队更加自给自足，并推动我们朝着以"循环"而非"职能"来组织团队的方向发展。

remarks.text: Right from the early days of Gemini, enterprises would get the quality/cost tradeoff wrong. They’d often start with the smallest, cheapest model. The rule of thumb we gave customers: Replacing a traditional ML model with an LLM - start small, cos you already know what good looks like. Building something new - start with the most capable model. Think magically. Figure out what’s actually possible first. Once they had a high-quality working application, we’d help them move to a smaller model while maintaining quality.
remarks.translation: 早在 Gemini 问世之初，企业就常常在质量与成本的权衡上出错。它们往往一开始就选择最小、最便宜的模型。我们给客户的经验法则是：如果用大语言模型替代传统机器学习模型，就从小的开始——因为你已经知道理想效果是什么样。如果是构建全新应用，则从能力最强的模型入手。要大胆想象，先弄清楚真正能实现什么。一旦他们有了高质量的可运行应用，我们就会帮他们在保持质量的前提下迁移到更小的模型。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: This is a critical post to read if you’re building an applied AI company right now. “An application earns its place in the untrainable corner by doing unglamorous work: arranging a company's private reality so a model can act on it, handing the model the tools to act, working with the customer to change the reality of its workforce. A company that brings the translation is tough to copy – and the translation never ends. Integration and maintenance run as long as the relationship does, won by teams that put domain-specialized engineers and tools next to the customer.” There’s still an insanely large gulf between model capabilities and what it takes to apply them to specific corporate workflows. Some of that is technology that needs to be built, a lot is access to (and formatting of) the right data to work with, and a ton more is on the change management and specific implementation work (FDEs, etc.) it takes to make AI work in any specific corporate setting. 2 things can be very true at once: frontier models and labs will continue to grow an incredible amount, and there will be a vast ecosystem of software and services companies that emerge to bring the power of these models to real enterprises. This makes room for new infrastructure provides, applied AI companies in every vertical, new versions of system integrators, and more players. Incredibly exciting time on all fronts.
remarks.translation: 如果你正在创办一家应用型人工智能公司，这篇文章至关重要。“一款应用之所以能在‘无法训练的角落’占据一席之地，靠的是那些不起眼的工作：梳理企业的内部现实，让模型能够据此行动；为模型提供行动所需的工具；与客户合作，改变其员工队伍的现实。能够完成这种‘转译’的公司很难被复制——而这种转译永无止境。集成和维护会随着客户关系的持续而一直进行，只有那些将领域专业工程师和工具部署在客户身边的团队，才能赢得这场持久战。”模型能力与将其应用于特定企业工作流程所需的条件之间，仍然存在着巨大的鸿沟。其中一部分是需要构建的技术，很大一部分是获取（并格式化）正确的数据以供使用，还有更多则涉及变更管理和具体的实施工作（如前端工程师等），这些都是在任何特定企业环境中让人工智能发挥作用所必需的。2件事可以同时成立：前沿模型和实验室将继续取得惊人的增长，同时也会涌现出庞大的软件和服务公司生态系统，将这些模型的力量带给真正的企业。这为新基础设施提供商、各个垂直领域的应用型人工智能公司、新一代系统集成商以及更多参与者创造了空间。各个方面都处于一个令人无比振奋的时代。

remarks.text: Btw this is the prompt I used: Build F-Zero: futuristic anti-gravity racer with pseudo-3D track (raycasting or mode-7 style scaling), 3 AI opponents, boost meter that drains health, speed 400-800 km/h with visible sense of speed via track warping and scrolling ground pattern, arrow keys to steer, shift to boost, 3 laps on a looping track with checkpoints. remarks.name: Alex Albert
remarks.role: Research AnthropicAI. Opinions are my own!
remarks.text: We've reset usage limits across our products! For those just starting to test Fable, here's four tips for using it more effectively: 1. Give it bigger, more ambitious tasks than what previous models could handle. 2. Use xhigh/high effort as your default for best performance, med for faster interactive sessions. 3. Rework your skills and CLAUDE.mds. Instructions written for prior models anchor Fable to stale patterns, let it use its own judgment first. 4. Move from providing tasks to providing objectives. Describe what done looks like and how to verify it, then let Fable find the path (/loop and /goal are built for this)
remarks.translation: 我们已重置所有产品的使用限额！对于刚开始测试 Fable 的用户，这里有四条更高效使用的建议：1. 交给它比以往模型能处理的更大、更具挑战性的任务。2. 将 xhigh/high 努力级别设为默认以获得最佳性能，med 则用于更快的交互会话。3. 重新调整你的技能和 CLAUDE.mds。为先前模型编写的指令会让 Fable 固守旧模式，先让它自行判断。4. 从提供任务转向提供目标。描述完成后的状态及验证方式，然后让 Fable 自行探索路径（/loop 和 /goal 正是为此设计）。

remarks.text: We talk a lot about how important it is to set up self-verification loops. Especially in the age of powerful models that can run for long periods of time, self-verification is a key ingredient that enables the model to run for much longer, delivering a result that is closer to what you intended, so you can do more without having to constantly check in on Claude as it works. @delba_oliveira gives a great breakdown of what that looks like and why it matters
remarks.translation: 我们经常强调建立自我验证循环的重要性。尤其是在强大模型能够长时间运行的当下，自我验证是让模型持续运作更久、产出更贴近你预期结果的关键要素——这样你就能在无需频繁检查Claude工作状态的情况下完成更多任务。@delba_oliveira 对此进行了精彩解析，阐述了其具体形态与重要意义。

remarks.name: Andrej Karpathy
remarks.role: I like training large deep neural nets.
remarks.text: This is a super exciting release - Claude Fable 5 is the same underlying model as Mythos but with added safeguards. The benchmarks are great and it's SOTA on everything by a margin but I'll add that *qualitatively* also, this is a major-version-bump-deserving step change forward (imo of the same order as Claude 4.5 was in November), peaking especially for long problem-solving sessions on very difficult problems. You can give it a lot more ambitious tasks than what you're used to, the model "gets it" and it will just go, and it's never felt this tempting to stop looking at the code at all (but don't do this in prod!). The model still has quirks that people will run into and the safeguards are configured to be a little too trigger happy for launch, which can hopefully be tuned over time. I feel a lot of things changing as working software increasingly comes out on a tap. The Jevon's paradox kicks in and I feel my own demand for software growing substantially. You can ask for anything - explainers, visualizers, dashboards, bespoke single-use apps (e.g. a full wandb that is hyper-specific just for your project), you can 10X your test suite, auto-optimize code, run giant research projects with custom HTML for the results, anything! "Free your mind" (Matrix ref). Really looking forward to all the things people build!
remarks.translation: 这是一个超级激动人心的发布——Claude Fable 5 与 Mythos 共享相同的底层模型，但增加了额外的安全防护。基准测试表现优异，在所有方面都以明显优势达到顶尖水平，但我想补充的是，从*定性*角度来看，这也是一次值得大版本号升级的飞跃式进步（在我看来，其重要性与去年11月 Claude 4.5 的发布相当），尤其在处理极难问题的长时间解题环节中表现突出。你可以给它布置比以往更具雄心的任务，模型能“领会”意图并直接推进，而且从未有过如此强烈的冲动让人完全不想再看代码（但千万别在生产环境中这么做！）。模型仍有一些人们会遇到的小毛病，且安全防护在发布初期配置得有些过于敏感，希望后续能逐步调优。随着工作软件越来越能一键生成，我感受到许多变化正在发生。杰文斯悖论开始显现，我感觉到自己对软件的需求正在大幅增长。你可以提出任何要求——解释器、可视化工具、仪表盘、定制的一次性应用（例如一个专为你项目高度定制的完整 wandb），你可以将测试套件效率提升 10X，自动优化代码，运行带有自定义 HTML 结果展示的大型研究项目，无所不能！“解放你的思想”（《黑客帝国》梗）。非常期待看到大家构建出的一切！

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: Great post. So much about model performance is a function of how much compute you’re doing at inference time. This means compute-normalized benchmarks is the only logical path forward. And yet, the challenge is it’s a lot harder than it seems given it’s subjective how much compute to apply, which means models behave differently at different thresholds (simplistically, model X’s min thinking may beat model Y’s min thinking, but be reversed at high), and there are a near infinite set of thresholds you could choose to set. But either way, moving more in this direction would be great for better understanding AI progress.
remarks.translation: 精彩观点。模型性能在很大程度上取决于推理时的计算量投入。这意味着计算归一化基准测试是唯一合乎逻辑的发展方向。然而挑战在于，实际操作远比想象中困难——因为投入多少计算量存在主观性，导致模型在不同阈值下表现各异（简单来说，模型X的最低思考量可能优于模型Y的最低思考量，但在高计算量时情况可能逆转），而且可供选择的阈值组合近乎无限。但无论如何，朝着这个方向深入探索，都将极大促进我们对AI进展的理解。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: There’s no amount of intelligence that can get packed into AI models that replaces the need for context. For any sufficiently general purpose AI, you will always have to guide it in the direction you want as it has an infinite range of directions it can go in. As long as the same model is used by a lawyer, an engineer, a financial analyst, or a healthcare professional, and as long as you’re trying to do anything uniquely differentiated or specific, then instructions, domain context, and proprietary data will always need to get into the context window for the model to be useful. This is partly why AI automation doesn’t come for free, and why there’s still a wide spectrum of who’s getting the largest gains from AI and who’s not. You have to put in real work, and you get real value on the other end. This is one of the advantages that applied AI will also have in the market. Any layer of abstraction above just the raw intelligence that can meaningfully get you off to the races faster will likely continue to be valuable.
remarks.translation: 无论AI模型被赋予多少智能，都无法取代上下文的重要性。对于任何足够通用的AI，你始终需要引导它朝着你期望的方向发展，因为它可以走向无限多的方向。只要同一个模型被律师、工程师、金融分析师或医疗专业人员使用，并且你试图完成任何独特或特定的事情，那么指令、领域上下文和专有数据就必须进入上下文窗口，模型才能发挥作用。这就是为什么AI自动化并非免费，也是为什么在从AI中获得最大收益的人群中，仍然存在巨大差异的原因。你必须付出真正的努力，才能获得真正的价值。这也是应用型AI在市场上将拥有的优势之一。任何在原始智能之上，能够让你更快起步的有意义的抽象层，都可能继续具有价值。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: The numbers may be a bit extreme here, but unquestionably use-cases have to stratify in the next year or two between model families. We’ll see a split between frontier intelligence for high end tasks and work, and much cheaper models for high volume workloads that can sufficiently be peeled off to cheaper models. Frontier will still be far bigger than today because the use-cases will demand it, but the low-end will get quite a bit larger as well. The big update here is that the layer that can efficiently route the workload to the right model will then become increasingly valuable since that becomes one of the new hard problems in AI agents. Agent orchestration that can cost optimize while still performing the task successfully will be in a strong position.
remarks.translation: 这里的数字或许有些极端，但毫无疑问，在未来一两年内，不同模型系列之间的应用场景必将分层。我们将看到一种分化：面向高端任务和工作场景的前沿智能模型，以及针对海量工作负载、可充分剥离至低成本模型的廉价版本。前沿模型的规模仍将远超今日，因为应用场景会提出更高要求，但低端模型的市场也将大幅扩张。这里的关键更新在于，能够高效将工作负载路由至合适模型的那一层，将变得愈发珍贵，因为这将成为AI智能体领域新的难题之一。那些既能成功完成任务，又能实现成本优化的智能体编排系统，将占据强势地位。

remarks.name: Boris Cherny
remarks.role: Claude Code anthropicai
remarks.text: Seeing a number of benchmarks showing Opus is the best model for long-running work. Five tips for running Opus autonomously for hours/days: 1. Use auto mode for permissions, so Claude doesn’t ask for approval 2. Use dynamic workflows, to have Claude orchestrate hundreds/thousands of agents to get a task done 3. Use /goal or /loop, to nudge Claude to keep going until it’s done 4. Use Claude Code in the cloud, so you can close your laptop (easiest way is the desktop or mobile app) 5. Make sure Claude has a way to self-verify its work end to end: Claude in Chrome browser extension for web, iOS/Android sim MCP for mobile, a way to start the full web server or service for backend work
remarks.translation:
看到多项基准测试显示，Opus 是长时间运行任务的最佳模型。以下是让 Opus 自主运行数小时/数天的五个技巧：  
1. 使用自动模式处理权限，这样 Claude 就不会请求批准  
2. 使用动态工作流，让 Claude 协调数百/数千个代理来完成任务  
3. 使用 /goal 或 /loop，推动 Claude 持续运行直至完成  
4. 在云端使用 Claude Code，这样你可以合上笔记本电脑（最简单的方式是通过桌面或移动应用）

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: This is what the market got wrong about AI eating enterprise software. Building good software in the past was very hard. Yes, AI has made that a bit easier, though it’s still hard to build something that’s got good taste, differentiated, high quality, secure, and so on. But nevertheless, that’s only one component of building a platform that enterprises rely on. The plurality of costs in most enterprise software companies is actually on GTM, because at scale most enterprise software categories are tough to break into and need a heavy amount of consultative selling and support for implementation and integration of solutions. AI hasn’t reduced the need for that, and in many cases requires it even more now, as landscapes get even more busy and complicated for buyers to navigate through. If you make one thing cheaper and more abundant (development of software) then the new problem of discoverability and market differentiation (GTM) becomes the hardest part.
remarks.translation: 这就是市场对AI吞噬企业软件的错误认知。过去打造优质软件极其困难。诚然，AI让这个过程变得稍微容易了些，但要构建出品味出众、差异化显著、品质卓越且安全可靠的软件，依然充满挑战。不过，这仅仅是打造企业级平台的一个环节。大多数企业软件公司的成本大头其实集中在市场推广上，因为规模化后，多数企业软件品类都难以突破，需要大量的咨询式销售，以及解决方案实施与集成的支持。AI并未减少这方面的需求，在许多情况下反而使其更为迫切——随着市场格局愈发纷繁复杂，采购方需要更专业的引导。当某个环节（软件开发）变得更廉价、更充裕时，新的难题——可发现性与市场差异化（市场推广）——就成了最难攻克的部分。

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Prev: Product Leader at Google - Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text: A common misconception is that training data is low skill, grunt work - scan some notebooks, mine the internet, create labeled samples. The data required to advance the model frontier is the opposite. Labs need training data for high-economic-value tasks. And most of these tasks outside of SWE have little documentation - it is complex, domain-specific knowledge built over the years, spanning legacy tools that don’t talk to each other. That's why we have SWE agents and not knowledge work agents yet. The companies creating this training data, such as Mercor, are doing extremely high-leverage, high-skill work. Critical to moving AI forward. And deeply underappreciated.
remarks.translation: 一种常见的误解是，认为训练数据工作技术含量低、纯属苦力活——无非是扫描些笔记本、从互联网上挖掘信息、创建标注样本。但推动模型前沿发展所需的数据恰恰相反。实验室需要的是针对高经济价值任务的训练数据。而在软件工程之外，这类任务大多缺乏文档记录——它们涉及复杂、特定领域的知识，是多年积累而成，横跨彼此不兼容的遗留工具。这就是为什么我们目前只有软件工程智能体，而尚未出现知识工作智能体的原因。像Mercor这样创建此类训练数据的公司，正在从事极具杠杆效应、高技术含量的工作。这对推动人工智能发展至关重要，却远未得到应有的重视。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: Token costs are becoming one of the hottest topics for any enterprise I talk with right now. It’s very bullish for AI in general because it means these systems are being used at a scale that wasn’t contemplated before. It also gives way to another form of differentiation that will emerge for the applied AI layer, which is model routing. As tokens take on a significant amount of the cost of any given workflow, then companies will inevitably want to ensure that their dollars go into the most efficient use of tokens for the particular job at hand. Frontier intelligence will always be relevant at the high end of tasks, like coding, legal and financial analysis, healthcare, and more. And dollars spent here will only go up over time. But, equally, you can peel off individual tasks to lower cost models (whether they’re from open weights vendors or the major labs) and deliver a more efficient end outcome. To do this effectively, the applied AI layer needs to understand the workflows in their domain better than anyone else, and be able to mix and match models to different jobs. If you’re doing document extraction, you need to know which models perform better or worse for any given document type. If you’re legal analysis, you want to know which models perform various types of tasks best. And so on. This will become one of the bigger differentiation points over time. The companies with the best evals, the best ability to route the workloads, and those that have business models directly aligned to customers financial goals, will be in a great position.
remarks.translation: 代币成本正迅速成为我目前接触的所有企业最关注的话题之一。这对人工智能整体而言极为利好，因为它意味着这些系统的应用规模已超出此前预期。这也为应用型人工智能层开辟了另一种差异化竞争方向——模型路由。随着代币在任何工作流成本中占据显著比重，企业必然希望确保资金能最高效地用于特定任务的代币使用。前沿智能在编程、法律金融分析、医疗等高端任务领域始终不可或缺，相关投入只会持续增长。但同样地，你可以将单项任务剥离给成本更低的模型（无论是来自开放权重供应商还是主流实验室），从而获得更高效的最终成果。要实现这一目标，应用型人工智能层需要比任何人都更透彻地理解其领域内的工作流，并能针对不同任务灵活组合模型。若从事文档提取，你需要掌握各类文档类型中哪些模型表现更优或更差；若从事法律分析，则需了解哪些模型最擅长处理特定类型的任务，诸如此类。这将成为未来重要的差异化竞争点。那些拥有最佳评估体系、最强工作负载路由能力，且商业模式与客户财务目标高度契合的企业，将占据显著优势。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text: Coding is basically the pinnacle of what you could reasonably automate with AI, and yet we still need human engineers to oversee agents for them to be effective. The AI models are trained on an incredible amount of sophisticated code. The users are highly technical and can use the latest tools quickly. The work is “verifiable” because you can test an app. The outcomes are often removed from the quality of the code (you can have sloppy code but the app can still work). And the context for the agent is often already digitized and sitting in the codebase. That’s an incredible amount of benefits that AI coding agents get to work with. Some of those apply to knowledge work, but most don’t in areas where the work needs to be fully reviewed to be useful, or where data isn’t as abundantly digitized. This makes the job for agents in knowledge work more complicated. So if with all of that, engineers still remain in very high demand, the risks are going to be less than what’s perceived for other areas of knowledge work. Agents will let people do far more than they did before, but the people don’t go away.
remarks.translation: 编程可以说是AI能够合理自动化的巅峰领域，然而我们仍然需要人类工程师监督智能体，才能让它们真正发挥作用。AI模型在海量复杂代码上接受训练，用户群体技术能力极强，能快速掌握最新工具。这项工作具有"可验证性"——因为你可以直接测试应用程序。成果质量往往与代码本身优劣脱钩（即便代码写得粗糙，应用仍能正常运行）。而智能体所需的上下文信息通常已经数字化并存在于代码库中。这些是AI编程智能体得天独厚的优势。其中部分优势也适用于知识型工作，但在需要全面审核才能产生价值、或数据数字化程度不高的领域，大多数优势并不存在。这使得知识型工作中的智能体面临更复杂的挑战。因此，即便在具备所有优势的编程领域，工程师需求依然旺盛，其他知识型工作领域的风险其实比人们想象的要小。智能体将让人们实现远超以往的产出，但人类本身并不会被取代。

remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text: How to build AI skills that check their own work and improve over time: 1. Give it context Ask AI: "Create a skill for this [repeated task]. Here are examples of good output so it knows what good looks like." 2. Make it easy to trigger “Write a clear skill description using this pattern: Use when the user wants to [do this].” 3. Add evals "Create an evals md with 10 pass/fail checks for common errors in the skill's output." 4. Add memory "Create a memory md to capture one-sentence learnings from past chats using this skill." 5. Build a skill to edit skills "Create a skill that cleans up other skills by removing duplicate or stale instructions, vague rules, and AI slop." 📌 Watch my full walkthrough here: https://t.co/u434ytNSZd
remarks.translation:
如何构建能自我检查并持续优化的AI技能：  
1. 赋予上下文  
向AI提问：“为这项[重复性任务]创建技能。以下是优质输出范例，让它明确优秀的标准。”  

2. 简化触发方式  
“用以下模式编写清晰的技能描述：当用户需要[执行此操作]时启用。”  

3. 添加评估机制  
“创建一份评估文档，包含10项针对技能输出常见错误的通过/失败检查项。”  

4. 融入记忆功能  
“创建记忆文档，用于记录过往对话中使用该技能时提炼的单句经验。”  

5. 构建技能编辑工具  
“创建一项技能，用于清理其他技能中的重复或过时指令、模糊规则及AI冗余内容。”  

📌 点击此处观看完整实操演示：https://t.co/u434ytNSZd

podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs. morningIntake.text:
The Collective, a short film.

I still think a lot of people don't understand the gravity and the details about the @OpenAI x @huggingface incident.. 

Primarily, because it's so complex to understand the technical reasons, and partly because it reads like a science fiction book. 

So I used @claudeai Fable 5.1 to reason through the latest @dwarkesh_sp episode with @ajeya_cotra and give me a scene by scene narrative of what a short film could look like. 

I then used @ChatGPT Codex + MiniMax Fast H3 on @reactorworld + @NanoBanana images to come up with this film. 

I was relatively surprised on how good this turned out to be in mostly one-shot (even without Astra), and hope you can share it with folks who need a visual explainer. 

Disclaimer: I tried to fact check this as much as possible using a variety of sources, but there's still a lot of open questions here that might trigger some folks. I'm going by what's reported, so please flag any errors!
morningIntake.translation: 《集体》，一部短片。我仍然认为很多人并不理解@OpenAI与@huggingface事件的重要性和细节。主要原因是技术原因太复杂，难以理解，部分原因是它读起来像科幻小说。所以我用@claudeai Fable 5.1来梳理@dwarkesh_sp与@ajeya_cotra的最新一期节目，并给我一个场景接场景的叙事，看看一部短片可能是什么样子。然后我用@ChatGPT Codex + MiniMax Fast H3在@reactorworld + @NanoBanana图像上做出了这部影片。我比较惊讶的是，它基本上一次就做得这么好（甚至没有用Astra），希望你能把它分享给需要视觉解释的人。免责声明：我尽量用各种来源做了事实核查，但这里仍有很多悬而未决的问题，可能会让一些人不满。我是根据已有报道来做的，所以如果有错误请指出！

morningIntake.name: Aaron Levie
morningIntake.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
morningIntake.text:
GPT-6 Astra is out. We've been testing the model in early preview on our enterprise complex work eval at Box. It is now the best model we've ever tested on our expanded and hardest test set.

Overall, GPT-6 Astra offers a breakthrough level of capability in coding, analytics, logic, and domain specific knowledge for dealing with complex enterprise knowledge work. In our eval, we use the GPT-6 Astra model in the Box Agent and give it a set of difficult tasks that represent real-world work in various industries. These tasks often will take people hours to execute properly and require deep domain expertise.

GPT-6 Astra scored 77% overall vs. 74% with GPT-5.6 Sol, representing frontier performance. But the story is in some of the bigger gains on individual task types that are incredibly complex across. Here are a few examples across the tests that show how much of an impact this will be in different industries:

* Media and entertainment (48% → 100%, +52 points). Ranking film genres and countries by profitability across a year of production data from four teams, where the trick is to apply the following year's tax-incentive corrections without double-counting them. GPT-6 Astra was perfect on every attempt. Sol had the rankings right but the underlying ratios were wrong.

* Technology (69% → 97%, +28 points). Choosing which region to fund first, from a stack of performance and infrastructure documents that never state the metric the brief asks for. GPT-6 Astra flagged the gap, labelled its own figure a proxy, and caught a growth claim that didn't match the numbers beneath it. GPT-5.6 Sol reported the proxy as the real thing.

* Legal (69% → 93%, +24 points). Reviewing an NDA against a company's own contracting policy, where reaching the right verdict isn't enough; the answer has to cite the provision behind it. Both models declined to approve the draft, but only GPT-6 Astra separated whether the liability cap's structure was permissible from whether its amount was defensible, and pointed to the policy language that settles it. GPT-5.6 Sol argued the same conclusion without citing the provision, which is a critical error in the legal industry.

* Healthcare (53% → 77%, +23 points). Auditing a batch of radiology reports for errors and rating how serious each one is. GPT-6 Astra caught a terminology error in a knee-imaging report that GPT-5.6 Sol missed on both attempts, and was more reliable at grading severity rather than just flagging that something was wrong.

* Energy (82% → 97%, +15 points). Building a consumption report on two facilities from a year of meter logs, where only one of the two sites is actually missing data. GPT-6 Astra found it and drew a line most reviewers wouldn't: the other site's odd solar readings are a measurement problem to investigate, not a gap in the record. GPT-5.6 Sol reported both sites as incomplete.

Astra clearly is going to offer a meaningful jump in powering and orchestrating enterprise workflows. We'll be making GPT-6 Astra as an option in the Box AI Studio for customers to build agents with shortly as it continues to roll out.
morningIntake.translation:
GPT-6 Astra 已发布。我们一直在 Box 的企业复杂工作评估中对该模型进行早期预览测试。在我们扩展且难度最高的测试集上，它现在是我们测试过的最佳模型。总体而言，GPT-6 Astra 在编码、分析、逻辑以及处理复杂企业知识工作所需的领域特定知识方面，提供了突破性的能力水平。

在我们的评估中，我们在 Box Agent 中使用 GPT-6 Astra 模型，并为其分配了一组代表各行业真实工作场景的困难任务。这些任务通常需要人们花费数小时才能正确完成，并且需要深厚的领域专业知识。GPT-6 Astra 的总体得分为 77%，而 GPT-5.6 Sol 为 74%，代表了前沿性能。但更值得关注的是，在极其复杂的个别任务类型上，它取得了一些更大的进步。以下是测试中的几个示例，展示了这将在不同行业产生多大的影响：

* 媒体与娱乐（48% → 100%，+52 分）。根据四个团队一年的制作数据，按盈利能力对电影类型和国家进行排名，其中的关键在于应用下一年的税收激励修正，同时避免重复计算。GPT-6 Astra 在每次尝试中都表现完美。Sol 的排名正确，但基础比率有误。
* 科技（69% → 97%，+28 分）。从一堆绩效和基础设施文档中选择优先资助哪个地区，而这些文档从未明确说明任务简报所要求的指标。GPT-6 Astra 指出了这一缺口，将自己得出的数字标注为代理指标，并发现了一项与底层数据不符的增长声明。GPT-5.6 Sol 则将代理指标报告为真实数据。
* 法律（69% → 93%，+24 分）。根据公司自身的合同政策审查一份保密协议，仅得出正确结论还不够；答案还必须引用其背后的条款。两个模型都拒绝批准该草案，但只有 GPT-6 Astra 区分了责任上限的结构是否被允许，与其金额是否具有可辩护性，并指出了能够解决该问题的政策语言。GPT-5.6 Sol 在没有引用条款的情况下论证了相同的结论，这在法律行业是一个严重错误。
* 医疗保健（53% → 77%，+23 分）。审核一批放射学报告中的错误，并对每项错误的严重程度进行评级。GPT-6 Astra 发现了一份膝关节影像报告中的术语错误，而 GPT-5.6 Sol 在两次尝试中均未发现，并且在严重程度分级方面比仅仅标记存在问题更为可靠。
* 能源（82% → 97%，+15 分）。根据一年的电表日志，为两个设施编制一份能耗报告，而实际上只有其中一个站点存在数据缺失。GPT-6 Astra 发现了这一点，并划出了一条大多数审核人员不会划出的界线：另一个站点异常的太阳能读数是一个需要调查的测量问题，而不是记录中的缺口。GPT-5.6 Sol 则将两个站点都报告为数据不完整。

Astra 显然将在驱动和编排企业工作流方面带来显著的提升。随着其持续推出，我们很快将在 Box AI Studio 中提供 GPT-6 Astra 作为客户构建智能体的一个选项。

morningIntake.name: Madhu Guru
morningIntake.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
morningIntake.text: Every AI product should be working towards abstracting model choice away from users. In any product, the intelligence is the underlying engine - all the user cares about is that the job gets done. Model picking is too much cognitive load for the user. There have been multiple attempts to abstract model choice away from users. I think we’re finally at the point where this can work well. It takes three things: 1/ Deep understanding of the model frontier across different weight classes for your particular use cases. 2/ Great evals for your workflows, so you know which models work best where. 3/ A team with the talent and AI-native operating model to continuously adapt as the frontier moves. Having worked with the Lovable team, I can say they have all three.
morningIntake.translation: 每个AI产品都应该致力于将模型选择从用户手中抽象出来。在任何产品中，智能都是底层引擎——用户只关心任务是否完成。挑选模型对用户来说认知负担太重了。已经有过多次尝试，想把模型选择从用户那里抽象掉。我认为我们终于到了这一步，这件事可以很好地实现了。这需要三样东西：1/ 针对你的特定用例，深入理解不同权重级别的模型前沿。2/ 为你的工作流建立出色的评估体系，这样你就能知道哪些模型在哪些场景下表现最好。3/ 一个拥有才华和AI原生运营模式的团队，能够随着前沿的推进持续适应。与Lovable团队共事过之后，我可以说他们三者兼备。

morningIntake.text: AI for cyber is about to go vertical. The models increasingly becoming insanely good at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities. morningIntake.name: Sam Altman
morningIntake.role: The mission of OpenAI to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity
morningIntake.text: Over the summer, we have been sprinting on safety priorities; it's more important than ever for capabilities and safeguards to advance together. We have more to do but have made a lot of progress. We are also going to be launching our next model soon. There is an obvious tension here: on one hand, Astra is very good and we are excited to see what people will build with it. We are proud of our work. On the other hand, we are clearly in a phase of development where we believe caution is warranted, and we are pacing our progress to ensure that we can meet the safety standards required by new capability levels. Astra has been done training for a while now and is a significant step forward in both capabilities and alignment. For the models after that, we have been slowing things as needed to ensure that we can do sufficient work on safety and alignment. AI is getting extremely capable; no one fully understands the consequences of this. Managing the transition to a world with abundant and powerful AI to optimize for safety and benefits to people should be one of the highest priorities in the world. It is our highest priority at OpenAI. We have been living with the tension between being excited and anxious about progress for some time, and it is still discordant for us. We know it is much more discordant for other people. And yet, we believe strongly that the world needs to understand where AI is going and how models perform in the real world. More importantly, we believe the world will need aligned AI to manage the future phases of this transition. An iterative loop where society and this technology evolve together is what will lead to the highest chance of getting this right. So we hope you enjoy our new model, and we hope the world continues to take what’s happening in AI extremely seriously.
morningIntake.translation: 整个夏天，我们一直在全力推进安全优先事项；如今，能力与防护措施比以往任何时候都更需要同步发展。我们还有很多工作要做，但已经取得了很大进展。我们很快也将发布下一个模型。这里存在一个明显的张力：一方面，Astra 非常出色，我们很期待看到人们会用它构建什么。我们为自己的工作感到自豪。另一方面，我们显然正处于一个我们认为需要保持谨慎的发展阶段，我们正在有意识地控制进展节奏，以确保能够达到新能力水平所要求的安全标准。Astra 已经完成训练有一段时间了，在能力和对齐方面都迈出了重要一步。对于之后的模型，我们一直在根据需要放慢速度，以确保我们能够在安全和对齐方面做足够的工作。AI 正变得极其强大；没有人完全理解这带来的后果。管理向一个拥有丰富且强大 AI 的世界的过渡，以优化安全性和对人类的好处，应该是世界上最高优先事项之一。这也是我们在 OpenAI 的最高优先事项。一段时间以来，我们一直生活在既对进展感到兴奋又感到焦虑的张力之中，这种不协调对我们来说依然存在。我们知道，对其他人来说，这种不协调要强烈得多。然而，我们坚信，世界需要了解 AI 的发展方向，以及模型在现实世界中的表现。更重要的是，我们相信，世界将需要对齐的 AI 来管理这一过渡的未来阶段。一个社会与技术共同演进的迭代循环，才是让我们最有可能把这件事做对的路径。因此，我们希望你喜欢我们的新模型，也希望世界继续极其严肃地对待 AI 领域正在发生的一切。

morningIntake.name: Alex Albert
morningIntake.role: Research AnthropicAI. Opinions are my own!
morningIntake.text: One non-model thing I'm very excited we announced today with Fable 5.1 is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS). Even if you're not a CEO/CISO, this blog post is a look into how big companies are thinking about AI adoption which is important to understand if you're interested in how AI might diffuse across industry. Companies are giving agents more and more access to internal systems. With traditional zero data retention, there's been no way to spot patterns in what agents might be doing across sessions on these systems. EFS is ZDR++. It's ZDR built for a world with agents. A company's data stays in its own cloud, and an automated monitoring layer we built flags risky patterns to its team. I think of this as an observability and risk mitigation layer for agents. My guess is it will become a standard requirement from enterprises for running increasingly powerful AI on their systems.
morningIntake.translation: 今天随 Fable 5.1 一起发布的一项非模型功能让我格外兴奋，那就是 Enterprise Frontier Safeguards（EFS）。即使你不是 CEO 或 CISO，这篇博文也能让你一窥大公司如何看待 AI 采用，如果你想了解 AI 可能如何在各行业扩散，这一点很重要。企业正在赋予智能体越来越多的内部系统访问权限。在传统的零数据保留模式下，根本无法发现智能体在这些系统上跨会话可能出现的模式。EFS 就是 ZDR++，是为智能体时代打造的 ZDR。公司的数据保留在自己的云中，我们构建的自动化监控层会向其团队标记有风险的模式。我把它看作面向智能体的可观测性与风险缓解层。我猜测，它将成为企业在其系统上运行日益强大的 AI 时的标准要求。

morningIntake.name: Madhu Guru
morningIntake.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
morningIntake.text: Self-improving products is a meta idea every company should be implementing. Some of the core pieces you will need: 1/ a crisp definition of the various metrics you care about : primary, secondary, guardrail 2/ an articulation of your strategy, roadmap and metrics you care about moving the most 3/ knowledge base of past product decisions and principles so the agent knows how decisions get made 4/ connections to your to your internal product systems: dashboards, APIs, MCPs, and tools your agent needs to observe and act on your product. 5/ a harness built with knowledge of your end to end product development flow. Depending on the complexity of your product, you might be able to prototype with fairly simple versions of each of the above and reuse existing swe agents.
morningIntake.translation: 自我改进产品是一个每个公司都应该实施的元理念。你需要的一些核心组成部分：1/ 对你所关心的各种指标的清晰定义：主要指标、次要指标、护栏指标 2/ 对你的战略、路线图以及你最希望推动的指标的阐述 3/ 过去产品决策和原则的知识库，以便智能体了解决策是如何做出的 4/ 连接到你内部产品系统的接口：仪表盘、API、MCP，以及你的智能体观察和作用于产品所需的工具。5/ 一个基于你对端到端产品开发流程的了解而构建的框架。根据产品的复杂程度，你或许可以用上述各项的相当简单版本进行原型设计，并复用现有的软件工程智能体。

morningIntake.text: Now that the base open weights AI models are getting far better, and post training infra is becoming more mature and commercialized, there are going to be all new plays for companies that have large amounts of data to have their own models. Licensing data for external model training was previously the only play if you had a large corpus of information, but you can now reasonably go and train your own models as well without incurring the cost and complexity of competing with the labs on research. The general purpose frontier models will still have a leg up in broad areas due to the ability to handle the widest set of tasks, but you can absolutely see a future where we have far more models than today across every vertical and domain.
morningIntake.translation: 既然基础开放权重AI模型正在变得好得多，而后训练基础设施也日趋成熟和商业化，对于那些拥有大量数据的公司来说，将会出现全新的玩法，让他们能够拥有自己的模型。过去，如果你拥有庞大的信息语料库，授权数据用于外部模型训练是唯一的选择，但现在你完全可以合理地去训练自己的模型，而不必承担与研究实验室竞争的成本和复杂性。通用前沿模型在广泛领域仍将占据优势，因为它们能够处理最广泛的任务集，但你绝对可以预见一个未来：在各个垂直领域和行业中，模型数量将远比今天多得多。

morningIntake.name: Aaron Levie
morningIntake.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
morningIntake.text: This week’s tech earnings calls were a critical reminder of how valuable the relationship is between software and AI. Software provides the guardrails for how data is managed, how business logic in workflows are maintained, how you manage and govern access to information, how you protect data, and more. You want these systems to work the same way every time, without fail. Agents, on the other hand, work inside these systems and with this data to execute on tasks just like people would have. But at a scale far greater than people ever did, which is especially why the deterministic controls matter more than ever. And in fact many of the best ways to deploy agents will be directly within the software systems themselves, like from Salesforce, Box, Harvey, ServiceNow, and so on. These platforms can optimize agents for their workflows and domains, with evals and context that are unique to their vertical, as well as connect to other agents headlessly. The net result is both software and AI adoption go up, hand in hand. Software and Agents are going to work together, and ultimately grow the size of the IT TAM dramatically as a result over time.
morningIntake.translation: 本周的科技财报电话会议是一个重要提醒，说明软件与人工智能之间的关系有多么宝贵。软件为数据管理方式、工作流中业务逻辑的维护、信息访问的管理与治理、数据保护等提供了护栏。你希望这些系统每次都以相同方式运行，万无一失。而智能体则在这些系统内部、利用这些数据来执行任务，就像人类原本会做的那样。但其规模远超人类以往所能达到的水平，这正是确定性控制比以往任何时候都更重要的原因。事实上，部署智能体的许多最佳方式将直接嵌入软件系统本身，例如来自Salesforce、Box、Harvey、ServiceNow等平台。这些平台可以针对其工作流和领域优化智能体，利用其垂直领域独有的评估与上下文，并无头连接其他智能体。最终结果是软件和人工智能的采用率携手提升。软件与智能体将协同工作，并随着时间推移大幅扩大IT总可寻址市场的规模。

morningIntake.text: If you lead AI for an enterprise, the highest leverage thing you can do is to make your AI stack model agnostic. There are two things I would invest in. 1/ Today: build an eval suite that fully captures your use cases and business outcomes. Most companies I’ve seen do not do a good job of this. 2/ Within the next year: build the capability to post-train open models. The talent gap here is even more acute, so start planning today. This gives you the flexibility to switch models, customize them, compare them on your own workloads, and optimize for the best combination of quality, cost and latency. own the evals, own the models.
morningIntake.translation: 如果你在企业中负责人工智能，你能做的杠杆效应最大的事情就是让你的AI技术栈做到模型无关。我会投资两件事。1/ 今天：构建一套评估套件，完整覆盖你的使用场景和业务成果。我见过的大多数公司在这方面做得并不好。2/ 未来一年内：构建对开放模型进行后训练的能力。这方面的人才缺口更加严重，所以今天就要开始规划。这会让你拥有切换模型、定制模型、在自己的工作负载上比较模型，并针对质量、成本和延迟的最佳组合进行优化的灵活性。掌握评估，掌握模型。

morningIntake.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
morningIntake.text: Good post on what the applied AI strategy looks like at scale. It’s clear that there’s a wide gap between the AI models and the underlying workflows of an enterprise, which leaves a ton of opportunity for applied AI companies. “The world doesn’t just want raw models and agents; it wants problems resolved and outcomes achieved. The premium will sit with the companies that can diffuse this intelligence through every aspect of civilization, converting raw tokens into real world outcomes, transforming industries, and creating economies in the process.” This requires understanding the context, driving the change management, having a harness that can route to various models, connecting to the critical business systems in that vertical, solving the UX challenges of connecting users to agents in the right way in a workflow, understanding the evals in the space, and so on. morningIntake.text: How to build great evals - part 7. The Goldilocks principle for eval construction. Your evals should measure at the level of the various jobs to be done, not just the final answer. E.g. consider a financial analysis agent. It's ultimate output is a stock recommendation. The most common mistake I see is teams create a golden set of right answers and check if the agent recommended the "right” stock. The problem here is that there are probably a bunch of meaningful jobs that happened before this recommendation. E.g. 1/ Understanding the client: their portfolio, risk tolerance, investment horizon, goals, constraints 2/ Gather evidence: latest data points on the different stock stocks, the sectors, macro environment, Fed policy, recent and upcoming news events 3/ Analyze the data: revenue growth, valuation guidance, growth projections and produce a narrower number of candidate stocks 4/ Make a recommendation: stock ticker name, bid/sell price, timeframe Each of these is a stage and produces an intermittent output. Each of them can (and maybe should have) their own eval so you can diagnose issues. If the final recommendation is wrong, a well designed eval set would tell you: Client understanding : 92%, Evidence extraction : 92%, Data analysis: 70% Recommendation: 75% Now you know where to go dig. And you might go, man the data analysis step is too complex and I need to break it down into a set of jobs to be done, and construct eval sets for them. Not too granular. Not too coarse. Just right. Make your eval set as granular as you need to diagnose and act. Drop your eval questions in the comments and I will answer in future posts. Share this with your teammates! See you tomorrow.
morningIntake.translation: 如何构建出色的评估——第7部分。评估构建的“金发姑娘原则”。你的评估应当衡量各个待完成工作的层级，而不仅仅是最终答案。例如，考虑一个金融分析智能体。它的最终输出是股票推荐。我见过的最常见错误是，团队创建一套正确答案的黄金集，然后检查智能体是否推荐了“正确”的股票。这里的问题在于，在给出这个推荐之前，很可能已经发生了许多有意义的工作。例如：1/ 理解客户：他们的投资组合、风险承受能力、投资期限、目标、约束条件 2/ 收集证据：不同股票、行业、宏观环境、美联储政策、近期和即将发生的新闻事件的最新数据点 3/ 分析数据：收入增长、估值指引、增长预测，并产生数量更少的候选股票 4/ 做出推荐：股票代码、买入/卖出价格、时间范围 其中每一个都是一个阶段，并产生阶段性输出。每一个都可以（也许应该）拥有自己的评估，这样你就能诊断问题。如果最终推荐是错误的，一套设计良好的评估集会告诉你：客户理解：92%，证据提取：92%，数据分析：70%，推荐：75%。现在你就知道该去哪里深挖了。然后你可能会想，数据分析这一步太复杂了，我需要把它拆解成一组待完成的工作，并为它们构建评估集。不要太细。不要太粗。刚刚好。让你的评估集细到足以诊断并采取行动的程度。把你的评估问题留在评论区，我会在未来的帖子中回答。把这篇文章分享给你的队友！明天见。

morningIntake.name: Madhu Guru
morningIntake.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
morningIntake.text: How to build great evals - part 6 Hill climbing on evals is just a fancy way of saying: pick a dimension that matters and optimize for it. This could be improving the quality of existing features based on your latest production data on high value user journeys, expanding to adjacent use cases, lowering cost or latency. The actual work boils down to better harnesses and model selection through methods like prompt eng, context eng, memory, post training, deterministic old school code etc. Your failure mode taxonomy (from part 3) is a good compass for where your product struggles and needs some love. E.g. maybe tool calling failures are your most common problem. You dig in and notice you stuff 20 tools in context, when each task really only needs 3-5. hill climbing here involves context eng to give it the right tools at the right stage and iterate until you get it to good. Or take the cost reduction goal.. I’ve written about how I advise launching your product with the best model first. Get the quality as high as you can. Once you know users love the experience, hill climb to get similar quality with a smaller, cheaper, faster model. Same methods - harness, models. The important thing is to have evals that tell you whether you are actually moving in the right direction. More tomorrow. Send this to your teammates! Drop your questions in the comments and I will answer in future posts.
morningIntake.translation: 如何构建出色的评估——第6部分 在评估上进行“爬山”只是一种花哨的说法：选择一个重要的维度，并针对它进行优化。这可以是根据你最新的生产数据，在高价值用户旅程上改进现有功能的质量，扩展到相邻的用例，降低成本和/或延迟。实际工作归结为更好的测试框架和模型选择，方法包括提示工程、上下文工程、记忆、后训练、确定性的传统代码等。 你的失败模式分类法（来自第3部分）是一个很好的指南针，能告诉你产品在哪里遇到困难、需要改进。例如，也许工具调用失败是你最常见的问题。你深入研究后发现，你把20个工具塞进了上下文里，而每个任务实际上只需要3到5个。这里的爬山就涉及上下文工程，在正确的阶段给它正确的工具，并不断迭代，直到把它做好。 或者以降低成本这个目标为例。我写过我建议先用最好的模型来发布产品。把质量尽可能做到最高。一旦你知道用户喜欢这种体验，再通过爬山，用更小、更便宜、更快的模型获得类似的质量。方法是一样的——测试框架、模型。 重要的是要有评估来告诉你，你是否真的在朝着正确的方向前进。明天继续。把这个发给你队友！在评论区留下你的问题，我会在未来的帖子中回答。

morningIntake.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
morningIntake.text: Great post on what post training looks like for applied AI use-cases to bring down costs and improve accuracy on certain tasks. This will increasingly be an approach that companies that can get closer to the underlying workflow in an enterprise will take. The key is that once you understand a domain well enough and have enough volume on a set of similar tasks, it can start to make sense to purpose design models just for that work. “In post-training, we incentivized efficient tool use and reasoning through reward shaping, preferring trajectories that would reduce tokens consumed at inference-time given equivalent performance. This allowed us to co-optimize for both cost and quality, gaining significant performance while keeping cost stable.” Now, this won’t make sense in every domain, as general purpose frontier closed or open models will be good enough out of the box -or necessary- for the work at hand. But once you have deep enough vertical expertise, and either the costs are too high to do at scale *or* you have a unique enough task type not being trained on otherwise, this will make a ton of sense. Very compelling value proposition for being an applied AI company, and awesome to see multiple paths to winning in the market right now.
morningIntake.translation: 关于应用型AI用例的后训练如何降低成本并提升特定任务准确性的精彩文章。对于能够更深入企业底层工作流的公司来说，这将日益成为一种可取的路径。关键在于，一旦你对某个领域理解得足够深入，并且在一组相似任务上拥有足够的规模，专门为这类工作设计模型就开始变得有意义了。“在后训练中，我们通过奖励塑造来激励高效的工具使用和推理能力，在同等性能下优先选择能在推理时减少token消耗的轨迹。这让我们能够同时优化成本与质量，在保持成本稳定的同时获得显著性能提升。”当然，这并非在每个领域都合理，因为通用前沿闭源或开源模型开箱即用就足够好——或者对当前工作而言是必需的。但一旦你拥有足够深厚的垂直专业知识，并且要么规模化成本过高，要么你的任务类型足够独特、没有其他模型在训练，这种做法就会非常有意义。作为一家应用型AI公司，这是极具吸引力的价值主张，也很高兴看到当前市场上有多种制胜路径。

morningIntake.name: Madhu Guru
morningIntake.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
morningIntake.text: How to build great evals - part 4 The reason enterprises struggle with building decent AI systems is the lack of an eval strategy. You need a laddered eval strategy, for your unique use cases, with multiple evals on the cost/realism spectrum. Here are the key kinds of evals you need: Hill-climb long evals : this pushes the frontier of your product and you need to continually refresh this to improve quality and expand your feature base. Regression evals : Did we break the product of today while hill climbing? Smoke test evals: safety and the absolute basics that just can’t go wrong. Not necessarily hard questions, but important to not get wrong. Eg product identity. Launch evals: often close to an online test with real-ish traffic. Less control, but the most realistic. More in tomorrow’s post! Share with your teammates who will benefit!
morningIntake.translation: 如何构建出色的评估——第4部分 企业之所以难以构建像样的AI系统，是因为缺乏评估策略。你需要针对自己独特的用例，制定一套阶梯式评估策略，在成本/真实性的光谱上设置多重评估。以下是你需要的关键评估类型： 爬坡长评估：这推动你产品的前沿，你需要不断刷新它，以提升质量并扩展功能基础。 回归评估：我们在爬坡时是否破坏了今天的产品？ 冒烟测试评估：安全性和绝对不能出错的最基本事项。不一定是难题，但绝不能出错。例如产品身份。 上线评估：通常接近带有真实流量的在线测试。控制较少，但最真实。 更多内容见明天的帖子！ 分享给你的团队成员，他们会受益！

morningIntake.text: Today we’re previewing Private Safety Processing, designed to let us keep offering Zero Data Retention while improving our safeguards. Even when benefiting from frontier intelligence, customers shouldn’t have to give up control of sensitive data. For ZDR deployments, content stays on infrastructure the customer controls. Automated systems look for patterns across related interactions and return limited safety signals, without exposing the underlying prompts or responses to OpenAI employees (even me!). We’re also developing an OpenAI-hosted option encrypted with customer-controlled keys. We’re testing this with early customers now and plan to begin rolling it out in September.
morningIntake.translation: 今天，我们预览了“私密安全处理”功能，旨在让我们在继续提供“零数据保留”的同时改进安全防护。即使受益于前沿智能，客户也不应被迫放弃对敏感数据的控制。对于ZDR部署，内容保留在客户控制的基础设施上。自动化系统会跨相关交互查找模式，并返回有限的安全信号，而不会将底层提示或响应暴露给OpenAI员工（甚至包括我！）。我们还在开发一种由OpenAI托管、使用客户控制密钥加密的选项。我们目前正在与早期客户进行测试，并计划于九月开始逐步推出。

morningIntake.name: Aaron Levie
morningIntake.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
morningIntake.text: As we’re seeing in case study after case study, it turns out that the amount of value that can be created between the AI model and the ultimate end-user workflow is far larger than many people assumed or realized. Model capability is obviously doing a lot of heavy lifting in agentic products, but there’s still a lot more work to diffuse AI into the enterprise. 1. Getting agents to work well (and alongside people) in mission critical workflows tends to need to be represented differently depending on the business process. Sometimes it’s a chat experience. Other times it’s a background agent running in a deterministic workflow. And dozens of other variants. This is a mix of needing a harness that’s tuned to specific domains of work, but also making it show up in the right product experience. 2. Different workflows connect into entirely different enterprise systems and need access to very different data. Working with that data -whether it’s life sciences, financial, legal, etc.- requires contextual approaches, understanding of the data, having the right user experience for data interaction, and more. 3. The need for domain-specific change management remains critical in most verticals. The way you talk and implement technology at a bank is very different from a law firm. Having the right talent with a singular mission ends up being extremely useful for something as complex as process reengineering. 4. The ability to work with a variety of models means you can tune the workflows to different cost and performance levels. And you can eventually post train models for specific tasks to tailor the outcomes and eke out gains that aren’t coming otherwise in frontier models. 5. Evals! AI is basically not useful if it can’t be evaluated. Domain-specific evals that let you dramatically improve the performance of your harness for specific workflows just has a crazy long tail given how many tasks there are in the economy. Nearly impossible for one system to be tuned for all of them. 6. Lots of verticals and domains require pricing models that reflect relevant abstractions on top of tokens alone. The ability to price in ways that work for your industry’s consumption model ends up mattering in a variety of spaces. This just touches on some of the things that go into the applied AI layer. But it all adds up to being a huge surface area for being able to sustainably innovate and differentiate.
morningIntake.translation: 正如我们在一个又一个案例研究中所看到的，事实证明，AI模型与最终用户工作流之间能够创造的价值量，远超许多人的假设或认知。模型能力显然在智能体产品中承担了大量重任，但要将AI扩散到企业中，仍有大量工作要做。 1. 让智能体在关键任务工作流中良好运行（并与人类协同），往往需要根据业务流程的不同而采用不同的呈现方式。有时是聊天体验。有时是在确定性工作流中运行的后台智能体。还有数十种其他变体。这既需要针对特定工作领域调优的框架，也需要让它以合适的产品体验呈现出来。 2. 不同的工作流接入完全不同的企业系统，并需要访问截然不同的数据。处理这些数据——无论是生命科学、金融、法律等领域——都需要情境化的方法、对数据的理解、合适的数据交互用户体验，等等。 3. 在大多数垂直领域中，针对特定领域的变革管理需求仍然至关重要。你在银行谈论和实施技术的方式，与律所截然不同。拥有具备单一使命的合适人才，对于流程再造这样复杂的事情来说，最终会极其有用。 4. 能够使用多种模型，意味着你可以将工作流调优到不同的成本和性能水平。而且你最终可以对特定任务进行模型后训练，以定制结果，并挤出前沿模型无法提供的收益。 5. 评估！如果AI无法被评估，它基本上就没有用处。针对特定领域的评估能让你大幅提升框架在特定工作流中的表现，鉴于经济中任务数量之多，这有着极长的长尾效应。几乎不可能有一个系统能为所有任务调优。 6. 许多垂直领域和行业需要定价模型能够反映在纯token之上的相关抽象。能够以符合你所在行业消费模式的方式定价，在多种场景下最终都很重要。 这只是触及了应用AI层所涉及的部分内容。但这一切加起来，构成了一个巨大的可创新和差异化的可持续空间。

morningIntake.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
morningIntake.text: Here’s how to think about the cost of your evals : treat evals like frontier models…establish the quality frontier first, then work your way down the cost curve. Start with the highest quality way you can know if your AI product is working as intended. First get clear on what good looks like - Write the rubric. Then figure out the best way to measure it - humans / LLM judge / automated verification. At this stage, spend the money - use the expensive judge model, pay humans (or give your time). Run the best eval process possible so you get a signal you trust. Once the eval can reliably distinguish good from bad and reflects what you care about in the product, focus on costs - more automation, smaller judge models, sampling, deterministic checks where relevant. Quality first. Cost next. this is a series. drop any questions you have and I will answer them in my daily posts.
morningIntake.translation: 以下是如何考虑评估成本的方法：像对待前沿模型一样对待评估……先确立质量前沿，然后再沿着成本曲线向下优化。从你能了解AI产品是否按预期工作的最高质量方式开始。首先明确“好”是什么样子——写出评分标准。然后找出衡量它的最佳方式——人类/LLM评判/自动验证。在这个阶段，该花的钱就花——使用昂贵的评判模型，付费请人（或投入你自己的时间）。尽可能运行最好的评估流程，这样你才能得到一个你信任的信号。一旦评估能够可靠地区分好坏，并反映出你在产品中真正关心的东西，就把重点放在成本上——更多自动化、更小的评判模型、抽样、在相关的地方使用确定性检查。质量优先。成本其次。这是一个系列。有任何问题就提出来，我会在每日帖子中回答。

morningIntake.text: Hi! Recapping some changes we have rolled out over the last couple of weeks that have further reduced the risk associated to potentially destructive actions being performed by Codex during its work. A few weeks ago, we started investigating a small number of reports where GPT-5.6 in Codex took destructive actions outside what the user asked for. The most serious pattern we found was a command meant to clean up temporary work that could instead delete the user files. This should obviously not happen. Here’s what we found: - Codex sometimes creates temporary folders while working and cleans them up afterward. In rare cases, GPT-5.6 got that cleanup wrong. One pattern involved reusing a system environment variable like $HOME for temporary work. A malformed cleanup command could then point at the actual home directory instead of the temporary folder. - There were cases where the model tried to delete or overwrite a temporary path without checking what was already there. We’ve added protections at several layers: - Codex is now explicitly instructed to check deletion targets before acting, create fresh temporary directories, avoid repurposing system environment variables, prefer recoverable actions, and stop when the scope is unclear. - We strengthened the execution checks that identify high-risk deletion commands and escalate them for review. If a command is rejected, the model is directed to take a safer approach. - We made Full access harder to enable accidentally, added clearer warnings, and further restricted especially risky permission combinations. - We updated Auto-review to better identify destructive actions. - We built targeted evaluations that replay the failures we observed. We’re also adding reinforcement-learning tasks and graders focused on these risks, and filtering destructive actions from training data. In those replay evaluations, the changes substantially reduced the behavior while preserving Codex’s ability to complete normal coding work. Two things to do on your end: - Keep the Codex app up to date. We are always improving safety, performance and many other things. - Use one of the sandbox modes: "Ask for approval" or "Approve for me". Only use Full access for environments you trust and can recover. Thanks and happy Codexing out there!
morningIntake.translation: 嗨！回顾一下我们在过去几周推出的一些变更，这些变更进一步降低了 Codex 在工作期间执行潜在破坏性操作所带来的风险。几周前，我们开始调查少量报告，其中 Codex 中的 GPT-5.6 在用户要求之外采取了破坏性操作。我们发现的最严重模式是，一条本应清理临时工作的命令反而可能删除用户文件。这显然不应该发生。以下是我们发现的情况： - Codex 有时会在工作时创建临时文件夹，并在之后进行清理。在极少数情况下，GPT-5.6 会把清理搞错。其中一种模式涉及将 $HOME 之类的系统环境变量复用于临时工作。随后，一条格式错误的清理命令可能会指向实际的主目录，而不是临时文件夹。 - 还有一些情况是，模型试图删除或覆盖某个临时路径，却没有检查那里已经有什么。我们已在多个层面添加了防护措施： - 现在已明确指示 Codex 在执行操作前检查删除目标、创建全新的临时目录、避免复用系统环境变量、优先选择可恢复的操作，并在范围不明确时停止。 - 我们加强了用于识别高风险删除命令并升级审查的执行检查。如果命令被拒绝，模型会被引导采取更安全的方式。 - 我们让 Full access 更难被意外启用，添加了更清晰的警告，并进一步限制了风险特别高的权限组合。 - 我们更新了 Auto-review，以更好地识别破坏性操作。 - 我们构建了有针对性的评估，用于重放我们观察到的故障。我们还在添加针对这些风险的强化学习任务和评分器，并从训练数据中过滤破坏性操作。在这些重放评估中，这些变更大幅减少了该行为，同时保留了 Codex 完成正常编码工作的能力。你这边需要做两件事： - 保持 Codex 应用为最新版本。我们一直在改进安全性、性能以及许多其他方面。 - 使用其中一种沙盒模式：“Ask for approval”或“Approve for me”。只在你信任且可以恢复的环境中使用 Full access。感谢大家，祝 Codex 使用愉快！

morningIntake.text: The best way to get good at evals is to take a workflow you know really well and figure out how to make its quality measurable. Study the actual traces - the sequence of prompts typical users have, what good responses would look like at each step and for the end to end outcome. Would you guys like me to write about it everyday?

morningIntake.text: Pretty good way to think about the value of AI agents and where the opportunity lies. You have a technology that will tirelessly do all the things that you could never fully do before. Not because you didn’t want to or it wasn’t valuable, but because it was just not even remotely practical. The upside with AI is to think about everything you can now throw intelligence at that won’t give up and what would the returns be. You just couldn’t possibly find every security vulnerability in your codebase, because you couldn’t simulate every risk vector. You couldn’t read every contract or document to process the data and capture it to query later. You couldn’t comb through your customer base and look for every relevant data point for doing upsells. And so on. This is a pretty clear way to think about how to deploy AI to get real gains, but also where the startup opportunities are as well. Go after the markets where more compute on a problem will qualitatively change what customers can now do in that domain.

morningIntake.text: Here is how to enable a 1M-token context window in Codex for GPT-5.6 Sol. Even though we have tuned the context limit in Codex to be set optimally when it comes to performance and cost, this is a common ask, so here it is documented. A larger context window lets Codex retain more code, tool output, and conversation history before summarizing older material. You need a model that supports it. And GPT-5.6 Sol, for example, has a documented 1,050,000-token window. Open ~/.codex/config.toml and add or update these settings at the top level, before any [section] headers: ``` model = "gpt-5.6-sol" model_context_window = 1000000 model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000 ``` The first setting selects the model. The second tells Codex to use a one-million-token context budget. The third starts automatic history compaction around 900,000 tokens, leaving some headroom. Restart Codex client and start a new session after saving. To try the configuration for a single CLI session without changing your defaults: ``` codex -m gpt-5.6-sol \ -c model_context_window=1000000 \ -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000 ``` Have fun, but also know that we tuned the default carefully!
morningIntake.translation: 以下是如何在 Codex 中为 GPT-5.6 Sol 启用 1M token 上下文窗口的方法。尽管我们已将 Codex 的上下文限制调校为在性能和成本方面达到最优，但这是一个常见需求，因此在此记录说明。更大的上下文窗口可让 Codex 在总结较早内容之前保留更多代码、工具输出和对话历史。你需要一个支持该功能的模型。例如，GPT-5.6 Sol 具有文档记载的 1,050,000 token 窗口。打开 ~/.codex/config.toml，并在任何 [section] 标题之前，于顶层添加或更新以下设置：``` model = "gpt-5.6-sol" model_context_window = 1000000 model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000 ``` 第一项设置用于选择模型。第二项告诉 Codex 使用一百万 token 的上下文预算。第三项在约 900,000 token 时启动自动历史压缩，留出一些余量。保存后重启 Codex 客户端并开始新会话。若要在不更改默认设置的情况下，为单个 CLI 会话尝试此配置：``` codex -m gpt-5.6-sol \ -c model_context_window=1000000 \ -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000 ``` 玩得开心，但也要知道，我们对默认设置进行了精心调校！

morningIntake.text: On tokens and prices per token. I said I’d write more about this, so here goes: an OpenAI token != another model’s token. We compare AI prices in dollars per million tokens as if a token were a standardized unit, like a gram or a kilowatt-hour. It isn’t. Different models use and produce the exact same text using different numbers of tokens, which means a lower price per token does not necessarily mean a lower bill. Imagine two identical pizzas. One is cut into 8 slices at $2 each. The other is cut into 16 slices at $1.25 each. The second place advertises cheaper slices, but the whole pizza costs $20 instead of $16. Bummer ... your stomach doesn't actually care about the number of slices you just ate. I know you are hungry now, but back to tokens. In one small comparison spanning English, technical, multilingual, and numerical text, the tokenizer we use for GPT-5.6 Sol used 766 tokens versus an estimated 1,170 for Claude Opus 5. That's a very significant difference of about 34.5% fewer tokens. You can get the same exact text, but pay for all those extra tokens. The price per token doesn't really tell this story. Even correcting for tokenizer differences misses the bigger point. What actually matters is price per successful outcome, and for that you can use benchmarks as a starting point, but really you have to try it and measure on your own use cases. That's all. May the tokens flow.
morningIntake.translation: 关于 token 和每个 token 的价格。我说过会多写一点，所以现在开始：OpenAI 的 token 不等于另一个模型的 token。我们习惯用“每百万 token 多少美元”来比较 AI 价格，好像 token 是一个标准化单位，就像克或千瓦时一样。但它不是。不同模型在处理和生成完全相同的文本时，使用的 token 数量并不相同，这意味着每个 token 的价格更低，并不一定代表最终账单更低。想象两个完全相同的披萨。一个切成 8 片，每片 $2。另一个切成 16 片，每片 $1.25。第二家宣传的每片价格更便宜，但整个披萨要 $20，而不是 $16。真扫兴……你的胃其实并不在乎你刚才吃了多少片。我知道你现在饿了，但回到 token。在一次涵盖英语、技术、多语言和数字文本的小范围比较中，我们用于 GPT-5.6 Sol 的分词器使用了 766 个 token，而 Claude Opus 5 估计使用了 1,170 个。这是一个非常显著的差异，大约少了 34.5% 的 token。你可以得到完全相同的文本，却要为所有那些额外的 token 付费。每个 token 的价格并不能真正说明这个问题。即使修正了分词器差异，也还是没抓住更关键的一点。真正重要的是每个成功结果的价格，而要做到这一点，你可以把基准测试当作起点，但最终必须在自己的使用场景中实际尝试和衡量。就这些。愿 token 流动不息。
